sentences.text:
-
1. Revision Petition filed by Central Bureau of Investigation Cri.Revn.310.24.odt 1 of 10 (CBI), Anti Corruption Branch (ACB), Pune, takes exception to order dated 13.07.2017 passed by Addl. Sessions The Police Inspector, Centraql Bureau ... vs Laxman S/O. Bhikaji Sonawane And Anr on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7006409/
1 Jude-5, Aurangabad on Application Exhibits 229 and 233 in Special Case No. 24 of 2008, by which the present respondent (original accused No.2) came to be discharged from offence under Sections 120B, 420, 468, 471 of Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC) and 13(1)(d) read with 13(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act.
2.

Learned Counsel for the Revision Petitioner Shri. Panale would apprise this Court about the factual background of the case, i.e. present Respondents working as Manager (Credit) and Branch Manager, Central Bank of India respectively.

He pointed out that report was received from one Regional Manager of Central Bank of India, namely, Shri. S. N. Basak regarding present respondents and five others conspired have used bogus bills for availing loan and credit facility in the name of unregistered firms by tendering bogus collateral security by way of mortgage and thereby cheated Central Bank India to the tune of Rs.1.5 crores.
3. He pointed out that on receipt of report to the above extent thorough inquiry was immediately made and on due Cri.Revn.310.24.odt 2 of 10 satisfaction matter was reported to CBI, ACB office Pune.

That therefore, after thorough investigation, it was revealed that after hatching conspiracy,
bank officials and private persons named in the report availed loan and credit facility on the strength of forged fabricated and bogus documents.

That statements of bank officials, Sales Tax Department and other departments were recorded and on due satisfaction, finding sufficient material against the accused persons, they were duly charge-sheeted.
That there was a case for accused persons to face trial, however, application for discharge came to be allowed by improperly appreciating the case advanced by the prosecution.
4. According to him, in spite of availability of sufficient material indicating conspiracy being hatched, documents were not being verified properly by the bank officials.
Thus, loans have been granted and bank is thereby being cheated which is in fact public fund and therefore, according to him, accused persons ought not to have been discharged.
5. Per contra, leaned counsel for Respondents would submit that present respondents are Manager (Credit) and Branch Cri.Revn.310.24.odt 3 of 10 Manager respectively.
He pointed out that accused No.1 and 3 are no more.
He pointed out that as regards the surviving accused No.3 is concerned, he was Manager (Credit) and was sitting at Regional Office in Aurangabad.
That the proposals were generated and processed to Udgir branch.
That duty of verification of documents and its authenticity was of other accused who are no more.
Even duty of granting sanction was of accused Shri. Gawai.
There are statements of auditor as well as one Naidu, Raghupati.

Therefore, according to him, learned Trial Court correctly appreciated the documents and rightly exercised his jurisdiction and discharged the accused and there was no material in the charge-sheet to make them face trial.
6. Perused the complaint which has resulted into registration of case against present respondents and others.

According to Shri. Basak, Assistant General Manager, Central Bank of India it was noticed during monitoring of the bank policy that large amount had slipped from Performing Assets to non Performing Assets from Udgir branch.
It was noticed that term loan and cash credit facility was extended in the name of M/s. Indrayani Milk & Milk Products Ltd., a unit located at Udgir.

2

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: According to him Cri.Revn.310.24.odt 4 of 10 due to some fraudulent acts of directors of said firm in connivance with the bank officials working at Udgir branch as well as at regional level at Aurangabad, the financial limit sanctioned was siphoned off and thereby, the branch had gone into financial losses to the tune of Rs.1.5 crores.

7. He further reported that during monitoring it was revealed that certain major irregularities in the accounts had occurred since inception itself and therefore, according to him the Head Office of the branch had decided to conduct internal investigation into the fraud and irregularities in detail and said task was assigned to vigilance section who tendered report that there was cheating to the tune of 1.5 crores by way of submission of false and bogus bills by M/s. Indrayani Milk & Milk Products Ltd., through its director, namely, M. D. Maramwar who had availed loan from the bank.

8. The report also names the bank officials who are responsible for the irregularities committed in the branch and they were Shri. G. P. Gawai, officiating as regional Manager, Central Bank of India,
Aurangabad; Shri. H. E. Gaikwad, the then Branch Cri.Revn.310.24.odt 5 of 10 Manager, Shri.L.B.
Sonawane (present respondent) Manager (Credit).
It was reported that role of such bank officials was apparent in the commission of the fraud.

9. The complainant has narrated the gist of the role of M/s. Indrayani Milk & Milk Products Ltd.,
Shri.Gaikwad, Branch Manager for forwarding recommendations for loan proposals of the said firm dishonestly and with malafide intentions not verifying the credit worthiness of the directors of the firm and viability of the project.

He reported that at regional office the proposal was also proceeded by Shri. Sonawane, Manager (Credit) and while processing it is alleged that he also did not deliberately examine the proposal in the context that already 3 to 4 milk daily projects were existing in the region and intentionally no comparative statement was processed by Shri. Sonawane to adjudge the viability and feasibility of the proposal of M/s. Indrayani Milk & Milk Products Ltd. .
Then there seem to be allegations against Shri. H.E. Gaikwad, Shri. Maramawar and others.

10. Thus, as regards the present Respondents Shri. Sonawane is concerned, there are allegations that he in spite of Cri.Revn.310.24.odt 6 of 10 being a Manager of Credit section and officiating at regional level in Aurangabad office did not examine the proposal and he rather processed the proposal.
Therefore, his role is specified in the complaint.
11. Perused the impugned order.

It seems that considering the submissions made by the parties before it, learned Trial Court has observed that there is no dispute regarding company submitting proposal for sanction of loan at branch, Udgir and the said proposal thereafter being forwarded to present respondent Shri. Sonawnae and it is observed that present respondent also verified and also made security of the documents and he further forwarded the recommendations for sanction to Shri. G. P. Gawai, who ultimately sanctioned the proposal.
.

Thereafter, learned Trial Court dealt with the provisions and requirements of 120A, 420, 468, 471 of IPC and reproduced the essential requirements in paragraph 10 and then in paragraph 11 observed that there are lapses on the part of accused Nos.2 and 3 while discharging their official duties.

3 12.

entities.text: Police Inspector, Centraql Bureau ... vs Laxman S/O. Bhikaji Sonawane And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Directly thereafter in paragraph 12 finding has been Cri.Revn.310.24.odt 7 of 10 recorded that considering the nature of allegations levelled against the accused and the ingredients of offences under Section 120B, 420, 468, 471 of IPC, held that prima facie it cannot be said that accused nos.2 and 3 had prepared forged documents and have used them as genuine having knowledge thereof that the documents were forged.
13 . Thereafter taking into account settlement proceedings before DRT, it is finally held that there was no proper reply from the prosecution to that extent.

Finally concluding in paragraph 18, it is observed that against accused, there could be charge of dereliction of duties which cannot be termed as criminal conspiracy, cheating or forgery as well as misconduct as contemplated under Section 13 of the Prevention of Corruption Act.

14. In the considered opinion of this Court, in the light of the nature of allegations levelled by the bank itself, it was too early for the leaned Trial Judge to express the opinion that the lapses on the part of bank officials would amount to at the most dereliction of the duty and nothing beyond that.

There was in fact material and even allegations are levelled that loan proposals have been received by Cri.Revn.310.24.odt 8 of 10 bank officials including present respondents and they were expected to verify the authenticity of the proposal, but the same does not seem to have matter.
15.
There are allegations of sanction of loan to the tune of 1.5 crores on the basis of forged and fabricated documents and even major irregularities are noticed since inception.
Head office before lodging complaint to ACB has also conducted internal investigation and has noticed irregularities and fraud being played on the bank.
Gist of the complaint against present respondents is also reflected in the de facto complaint.

Resultantly, learned Trial Court ought not to have merely by reproducing essentially ingredients of the offence, form opinion that the act of the accused would amount to mere dereliction of duty, and ought not to have discharged the accused.
In fact there was material both in the complaint as well as statements of bank officials to proceed for framing charge.

The aspect of settlement before DRT also seems to have prevailed over the learned Trial Judge in granting discharge which, in the considered opinion of this Court was not proper.
.
For above reasons, Criminal Revision Application is Cri.Revn.310.24.odt 9 of 10 required to be allowed by setting aside the impugned order.

Hence, the following order:
ORDER . Criminal Revision Application is allowed in terms of prayer clause 'B'.
( ABHAY S. WAGHWASE, J)
